title: Severe Bleeding & Tourniquet
summary: Apply firm direct pressure. For life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg that pressure does not control, apply a tourniquet and note the time.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for any severe bleeding
when: Blood is spurting, pooling or soaking through dressings
Signs of shock: pale, cold, clammy, fast breathing, confused
Wound to the head, neck, chest, abdomen or groin

steps.title: Protect yourself and call for help
steps.text: Wear gloves if available. Call {EMERGENCY} or get someone else to call. Get a bleeding control kit or first aid kit.

steps.title: Apply firm direct pressure
steps.text: Press firmly directly on the wound with a dressing, clean cloth or your gloved hand. Keep pressing hard and do not lift to check.
points: Use a haemostatic (blood-clotting) dressing if you have one and are trained
If blood soaks through, add more dressings on top and keep pressing

steps.title: Tourniquet for life-threatening limb bleeding
steps.text: If bleeding from an arm or leg is life-threatening and direct pressure does not control it (or you cannot keep pressure on, e.g. several casualties), apply a manufactured tourniquet.
points: Place it 5–7 cm (2–3 in) above the wound, not over a joint
If the wound location is unclear, place it high on the limb
Note the time it was applied
steps.caution: Applying a tourniquet properly hurts. Keep tightening until the bleeding stops.

steps.title: If bleeding continues
steps.text: If one tourniquet does not stop the bleeding, apply a second one above the first. If you have no tourniquet, keep up firm direct pressure.
steps.caution: Improvised tourniquets often fail. Use a manufactured tourniquet if available.

steps.title: Wounds to the body, neck or groin
steps.text: Tourniquets cannot be used here. Pack deep wounds with gauze (haemostatic gauze if available) if trained, then press firmly and keep pressing.

steps.title: Treat for shock and monitor
steps.text: Lay them down, keep them warm and reassure them. Watch breathing and response. Tell the responders the time the tourniquet was applied; write it on the casualty or tourniquet if you can.

warningSigns: Fast, weak pulse or fast breathing
Bleeding that won't stop with pressure
doNot: Do not remove a tourniquet once applied – leave it for medical staff
Do not loosen a tourniquet to 'check' or to relieve pain
Do not remove objects embedded in a wound – pad around them
Do not lift dressings to check whether bleeding has stopped

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)
